page.layout: One column of running text, with two small printed marginal notes in the right margin beside the first numbered paragraph. Nothing below the text except the catchword at the right.

main_text.p: gus ab aqua proveniens ibi dominatur: ex quo fit, ut flatus Austrini calor vix in pontum penetret. Atqui provenit ibi calor quidā intrò coactus per ἀν-τιπερίστασιν[?] (quasi dicas, contrariorum circumstantiam) à frigore undique circumambiente, & Borea prævalente. Itaque talis calor quando vi circumfusi frigoris excitatur, tum ros producitur.
main_text.head: Quæ sunt causæ nivis?
main_text.p: 1. Causa materialis, vapores. Eadem plane mate-Libro I.ria est nivis, quæ & primæ: verum nivis materia cap. II.altius subvehitur.

2. Causa formalis: Eodem pacto procreatur nix, quo pruina. Etenim proportio & ἀναλογία[?] magna est nivis cum pruina, sicut & pluviæ cum rore. Nix namq; & pruina gignuntur tantum tempore ac locis frigidis, sicut ros & pruina tempore ac locis sub-calidis. Hæc autem, ut rectius iudicemus de causa nivis formali, sunt observanda discrimina: Pluvia sublimiore loco & ex crassiore provenit materia (nempe à magnis nubibus) eademq; longiore temporis spacio collecta: ros vero loco humiliore ex materia tenui, & tanquam ex nebulis, & sursum cue-cta unius diei spacio. Ad eundem modum nix quoq; loco sublimiore ex materia corpulenta & paula-tim collecta procreatur: pruina vero loco hu-miliore ex materia exili & celeri-ter è terris educta.

page.notes: Page number at the head right is faint and read as 313 with doubt. Greek words ἀντιπερίστασιν and ἀναλογία are uncertain in their accents and letters. The two marginal notes "Libro I." and "cap. II." are small and partly rubbed. Show-through from the other side is visible in the lower margins and is left out. The top-left fragment "gus" is the end of a word from the previous line of the printed page and is kept as a fragment.
